title: Most People Miss This About Hagar Encountering God
paragraphs: Most People Miss This About Hagar Encountering God
She wasn’t supposed to be the one God spoke to.

Not the wife.
Not the chosen line.
Not the promise-holder.
Hagar was the outsider… used, discarded, and running for her life.

Alone.
Pregnant.
Rejected.
And that’s where it happens.
In the wilderness—no altar, no priest, no audience—God shows up.
But here’s what most people miss…
Hagar doesn’t just hear God.
She names Him.

“El Roi.”
The God who sees me. (Genesis 16:13)
Pause there.
This Egyptian slave woman—wounded, invisible in everyone else’s story—becomes the first person in Scripture to give God a name.

Not Abraham.
Not Sarah.
Not kings or prophets.
Her.
Why?

Because broken places don’t repel God.
They attract Him.

We expect God in temples.
He walks into trauma.

We look for Him in strength.
He reveals Himself in survival.
And here’s the deeper cut—
Hagar wasn’t even part of the covenant line that would lead to Jesus.
But God still pursued her.
That means this isn’t just about history.
It’s about you.

You who feel unseen.
Used.
Left out of the “main story.”
God sees you.

Not the curated version.
Not the filtered life.
You.
And He doesn’t just see—He speaks.
But here’s where grace breaks in fully—
Hagar’s story whispers forward to a greater moment.

Another rejected One.
Another suffering outside the camp.
Another who was seen as nothing.
Jesus Christ.
On the cross, He carried every moment you felt invisible… and made a way for you to be fully known and fully loved.
Not because you earned it.
But because He chose you in your wilderness.
So if you’re there right now—

Running.
Hiding.
Barely holding it together—
Lift your eyes.
El Roi is not distant.
He is near.
And in Christ, the God who sees you… also saves you.
Someone you know is walking through a silent wilderness.
